newsitem.title: USA: Unocal refineries run ahead of strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Unocal refineries run ahead of strike threat.

text.p: Union workers remained on the job at four Unocal Corp California refineries early Monday, ahead of a threatened strike, the company said.
In a letter to Unocal late last week, the Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) threatened to terminate its contract late Monday, giving workers the option to strike.
"They're still working," said Unocal spokesman Barry Lane, referring to the 900 union workers at Unocal's refineries.
Unocal's Lane said the company continues to talk to the union informally, despite the end of formal negotiations last week.
"At this point, we don't believe there will be a stike," Lane said.
Separately, union officials were expected to meet with Tosco Corp later today.
Tosco will assume ownership of the facilities on March 31. Tosco's contract negotiations with the union stalled last week over a new labor contract.
"Things are on the move. It's promising," said Howard Spencer, a union official.
